prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of magic-angle flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle

statement.case_for: I keep B016 as my preferred configuration after the full first-round exchange. The scientific case is a direct chain: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that a continuum moire model has nearly flat bands at a magic twist angle, and the 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulating states and superconductivity at that angle. The model is the one the experiment tested, the phenomena have been reproduced by many independent groups, and the platform has generalised to other moire systems. In response to the chair's own question about the citation, I would word it narrowly around the flat-band prediction and the discovery of the correlated insulating and superconducting states, and say nothing about the pairing mechanism. That wording rewards what is established and leaves the open physics open. Having read the round-1 files, I find the B048 attribution problem was not resolved by the supporters, only reframed, whereas the B016 attribution gap is of a more routine kind.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains maturity. Seven years after the 2018 experiments the pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated insulators are still debated, and Eriksson and I are the only two members who prefer B016 despite its breadth of opening support, which tells me the committee is not convinced it is ready. Attribution is imperfect: Yuan Cao and the other co-first authors, Dean and collaborators, and earlier continuum-model theory by Santos, Peres and Castro Neto sit outside the three names. B049 has more than twenty years of confirmation and a cleaner two-name credit, and if the committee decides that a prize should not precede a settled mechanism, B049 is the better answer, not a patched B048.

responses.point: Danielsson holds that B048 can be cited around the Z2 state and its first observation, and that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is a materials step between Kane-Mele and Molenkamp that three names need not repair.
responses.response: I understand the wording strategy, but I do not think it is neutral. Molenkamp's HgTe result is an experimental test of the BHZ proposal for HgTe wells, not of the Kane-Mele graphene model, whose spin-orbit gap is far too small. A citation that credits the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation to the same three people asserts a link that the physics runs through someone else. You said yourself that you cannot say which of the three would give way, and I take that as the honest answer. I have moved closer to your view on maturity, which is why B048 is my first alternative, but I have not moved on attribution.

responses.point: Olsson says that if the committee thinks BHZ is essential, the honest alternative is a different prize and not a patched one, and that the B048 citation should rest on the conceptual advance and not on applications.
responses.response: I agree with the principle you state, and I apply it to B048 and to B016 alike. If the attribution gap cannot be closed within three names, choose a prize where it can be managed. For B016 the gap is managed because the prediction and the experiment concern the same model, and the co-first-author question is one the committee has handled before. I also agree with your point about applications: my B016 citation says nothing about devices or about a pairing mechanism. Where we differ is the weight of the 2016 overlap and breadth. I do not treat breadth of opening support as decisive for B048, since B016 has seven rankers against six.

responses.point: Lindroth asked whether a B048 citation can be drafted that is accurate about who predicted what in HgTe, and keeps B049 first while treating the redefinition of the second as a timing signal in favour.
responses.response: Your drafting question is the one I cannot answer for B048, and I notice that no supporter drafted such a citation in round 1; they restated the Z2-and-first-observation formula instead. On B049 I accept your argument that magic-wavelength trapping changed the statistical regime and is not simply a better trap, and I accept that the credit is clean. My remaining hesitation is smaller than in round 1 but real: the redefinition of the second has not happened, and early lattice-clock priority (the Lemonde group, the JILA and Tokyo teams) rests on recollection that neither of us can verify here. For that reason B049 stays an alternative, ahead of any B048 repair.

responses.point: Kroll argues that lattice clocks have no recent prize and no attribution squeeze, and asks whether IceCube (B047) outranks them; he also flags a possible recusal discussion from his time in Hall's laboratory.
responses.response: On IceCube I am settled: I do not carry B047 forward, as only Danielsson and I ranked it and the single-name credit for a large collaboration is a real defect. I accept your point that B049 has no attribution squeeze. I would not ask you to recuse, since a stay in a laboratory associated with JILA is a field connection and not a collaboration with Katori or Ye, but the committee should weigh your statement as that of an atomic physicist, as you note yourself. Where we still differ is on novelty after 2005 and 2012: I take your answer that many-atom operation without a first-order light shift is a new principle, yet I think it is the point on which the committee is most likely to split.

uncertainties: Whether seven years of confirmation is enough given the unsettled pairing mechanism, or whether the committee should wait for the mechanism before honouring B016.
How to treat Yuan Cao and the other co-first authors of the 2018 experiments, and Dean and collaborators, within a three-person limit.
Whether a B048 citation can honestly be drafted without Bernevig, Hughes or Zhang; I have not seen a draft that does so, and I rely on recalled history of the HgTe proposal.
Whether B049 priority among early lattice-clock proposers is settled, and whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to act or to wait.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B016, B048 or B049. My documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) involve none of the credited names. I withdrew from B047 in round 1 and do not carry it, so the field proximity I noted for the IceCube candidate no longer bears on my configuration. I do not ask for any other member to recuse; Johansson's and Kroll's disclosures are for the committee to weigh.
